title: Brave’s browser one-ups Chrome with its new support for email aliases
slides: Brave challenges Chrome, but can it fix email privacy?
New email alias support hides your real address.
Chrome lacks this; Google profits from your inbox.
You now shield your email from trackers automatically.
Try it today: switch your default browser to Brave.
thread_text:
1. Your inbox is exposed.

Brave's new email alias feature hides your real address, a move Chrome hasn't made. Google's business model profits from scanning your inbox.

2. Trackers, meet your match.

Brave automatically shields your email from trackers, something Chrome lacks. Your address stays private without extra steps.

3. Why Chrome stays silent.

Google profits from your inbox data. Brave's challenge to Chrome isn't just about browsing—it's about who owns your email.

4. One switch, zero effort.

Switching your default browser to Brave activates email protection instantly. No settings to fiddle with—just a change of default.

5. Ready to protect your inbox?

Switch your default browser to Brave today. Or ask yourself: why keep a browser that profits from your private emails?

instagram.caption:
Your real email address is sitting in every login form you've ever filled—and that's exactly what trackers exploit.

Brave just added email alias support to its browser, hiding your actual address behind a randomly generated one. Chrome has no equivalent, and Google's business model profits from reading your inbox. 🔒

This isn't about privacy theater. It's a direct upgrade to how your personal data flows every time you sign up for a newsletter or tool.

For anyone creating content, that means fewer tracking pixels connecting your email across platforms. One switch in settings, and future signups are masked automatically. ✉️

When did you last get a cold email that knew exactly what you'd been browsing? 🧐
